- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; apply downward bias of 2–5% to prevent overshoot.
- If true price declines sharply from recent peak, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in downward movement.
- In multi-day downtrends, model tends to underestimate early; apply upward bias to first 3–5 days of forecast to capture mean reversion.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply 2–4% downward correction in first 2–3 days of forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 2–5% downward adjustment if sentiment >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If true price drops below 60% of recent high, model often fails to recognize it; apply 3–5% upward bias to prevent underestimation in early days of decline.
